title: Care Desk Guidance Note: Consolidating and Giving Away Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards
content:
A transfer between Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards always moves the whole balance of one card onto another card of the same customer. It is booked as a transfer out of that amount on the source card and a transfer in of the same amount on the receiving card, each entry naming the other card as its counterpart; the source card number then closes.

Consolidation onto a reloadable Marlowe & Finch Gift Card is allowed only where both card kinds can be consolidated and the result stays within the receiving card's largest balance after reloads. Registry Reward Cards and Marlowe & Finch Bonus Cards are never consolidated. The receiving card keeps its own rules, so value from a card that would expire never gains an expiry by consolidation.

A card can be given to someone else only where its kind is transferable; a Registry Reward Card and a Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card stay with the customer named on them.

## The terms in parts

| Matter | Position |
|---|---|
| How much moves | The whole balance of the source card, never part of it |
| Between whom | Two cards of the same customer |
| How it is booked | A transfer out on the source card and a transfer in of the same amount on the receiving card, each naming the other as counterpart |
| Onto a reloadable Marlowe & Finch Gift Card | Only where both kinds can be consolidated and the result stays within the receiving card's largest balance after reloads |
| Registry Reward Card or Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card | Never consolidated |
| Rules after the move | Those of the receiving card |
| Giving a card to another person | Only for a transferable kind; a Registry Reward Card and a Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card stay with the customer named on them |

## Hypothetical cases

- A hypothetical customer holds a Merchandise Credit Card with $42.50 and a reloadable Marlowe & Finch Gift Card with $300.00. Both kinds can be consolidated, and $300.00 together with $42.50 is $342.50, within the receiving card's largest balance after reloads of $2000.00. The whole $42.50 leaves the Merchandise Credit Card as a transfer out naming the Gift Card, the Gift Card receives a transfer in of $42.50 naming the Merchandise Credit Card, and the Merchandise Credit Card closes.
- The same customer asks to move only $20.00 of the $42.50. A transfer always moves the whole balance, so a part-balance move is not a transfer under these terms.
- A hypothetical Gift Card holding $1980.00 would receive $42.50, giving $2022.50, which is above its largest balance after reloads of $2000.00; that consolidation is not allowed.
- A hypothetical Registry Reward Card holding $60.00 is never consolidated onto another card, and it stays with the customer named on it.
